title: 4.1.5 Q1 Synthesis Design Plan
description: Design day: plan the whole program as numbered pseudocode before any build time. One CALL per planned function, under twenty steps. The build lessons open when this is green.

steps.title: Write the plan for your whole program
steps.instructions:
Plan the **whole program** before writing any of it. **No JavaScript is written today.** The build lessons stay closed until this plan is green.

From the project checklist, your program has to:

- store at least five objects of your own design in an array
- write a function of your own with at least 3 parameters
- write a function of your own that returns a computed value, used elsewhere in the program
- sort the array
- read the array with a loop
- make a decision with a conditional based on your data
- save and load your data
- print one formatted verdict line combining at least two things you calculated

In `README.md`, write the **main program** as numbered pseudocode **between START and END**: the sequence that runs when the page loads. Number every line, including the indented ones and the END lines. Each keyword looks like this:

- `CALL loadQueue` (one line for each function you plan to write)
- `IF there is a saved queue` ... `ELSE` ... `END IF` (a decision, with both ways out)
- `FOR EACH order IN queue` ... `END FOR` (walking your array)
- `OUTPUT the verdict line` (the printed result)

Three rules make it a design. **One CALL per planned function, both directions**: every function you intend to write is on the plan, and every CALL becomes a real function. **Stay under twenty steps**: if you cannot, collapse a run of steps into a function and name it. **Do not write the function bodies**: only the main program.

When you hand in the finished project, the plan comes with it and one thing is compared: does the code match the plan? You may change your mind. What is not allowed is silently abandoning the plan: update it and say in your README what changed and why.
hints: Every function you plan to write is one CALL line. Do not write what is inside it.
A decision needs both ways out: an IF with an ELSE.

requirements.title: Ten or more numbered steps
requirements.description: Number every line 1. 2. 3. and so on. A plan under ten steps has not been decided yet.
requirements.hint: You need at least ten numbered lines, one after another. Number the indented ones and the END lines too. Keep it under twenty: collapse a run of steps into a function.

requirements.title: A decision with both ways out
requirements.description: An IF closed with END IF, with an ELSE for the other way.
requirements.hint: Add a decision, for example "is there saved data?": IF ... ELSE ... END IF. A decision with one exit is only half a decision.

requirements.title: A loop over your array
requirements.description: FOR EACH item IN list ... END FOR.
requirements.hint: Walk your array with FOR EACH item IN list ... END FOR.

requirements.title: Functions planned as CALL lines
requirements.description: At least three CALL lines: one per function you plan to write.
requirements.hint: Write one CALL line for each function you plan to write, at least three.

requirements.title: Sorting, saving and loading are planned
requirements.description: A CALL for each: something with sort, something with save, something with load.
requirements.hint: Plan a CALL for sorting, one for saving and one for loading, for example CALL sortByPriority, CALL saveQueue, CALL loadQueue.

requirements.title: One verdict line is printed
requirements.description: An OUTPUT (or PRINT) line for the formatted verdict.
requirements.hint: End with an OUTPUT line for your formatted verdict.
